summary: Admit approval-bound Russian Post batch handoff through the tenant-scoped API and durable idempotency receipt boundary.

impacts.evidence: The API resolves the active connector account inside the authenticated organization/workspace scope and the operation receipt is tenant-scoped.
Only the normalized submission projection is stored; credentials, provider response bodies and recipient data remain outside the durable result.
OpenAPI adds POST /logistics/batches/{batch_id}/submit with required Idempotency-Key and Approval-Request-ID headers and a bounded request schema.
The operation returns a normalized response and does not add or change an event contract.
The provider-neutral LogisticsBatchSubmitRequest, LogisticsBatchSubmission and submitter port add one capability without exposing Russian Post transport types.
The existing operation_receipts schema already supports pending/completed tenant-scoped idempotency results; no migration is required.
The write-sensitive operation is default-deny, requires an enabled account capability and validates the exact normalized batch reference before accepting the provider response.
The route requires an approved fulfillment.batch.submit request bound to the canonical batch/options digest and write-sensitive risk class.
Approval and idempotency identifiers are bound to the request digest and tenant-scoped receipt, preserving durable mutation lineage without raw provider payload.
A fresh receipt owns the one remote check-in; completed replays return the normalized result and pending receipts block automatic duplicate submission.
The adapter egress is fixed to the official HTTPS Otpravka check-in endpoint and sends only the documented optional query flag.
The API distinguishes fresh accepted results, completed replays and pending ambiguous outcomes while mapping provider failures without exposing response bodies.
Disabling the capability or removing runtime admission prevents new handoffs; existing pending/completed receipts remain available for reconciliation and audit.
Deterministic connector, HTTPS transport, API approval/idempotency, runtime admission, OpenAPI parity, generated SDK and frontend checks cover the new operation.
